summary.intent: Avoid a per-request load_verify_locations() when verify=True by passing a module-level SSLContext with the default CA bundle preloaded, and by no longer setting ca_certs/ca_cert_dir on the connection in that case.
summary.issue_fit: Partial — the performance goal is met, but verify=True combined with a client certificate now loads that certificate into the shared context. No originating issue exists; intent comes from the supplied pull-request text and the four commit messages.
summary.coverage: Complete merge-base diff of `src/requests/adapters.py` reviewed with urllib3 2.8.0 callers. Scratch reproductions at the head and merge-base support both findings. Focused ssl/verify/cert/pool selection ran once at the head: 16 passed, 3 failed (`test_pyopenssl_redirect`, `test_different_connection_pool_for_tls_settings_verify_bundle_unexpired_cert`, `test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings`); the first two are known merge-base failures, and the third fails at the merge-base too with an expired-certificate fixture error. The >100% speedup claim was not measured (no network).

findings.title: Stop loading client certificates into the shared default SSLContext
findings.trigger: `requests.get(url, verify=True, cert=(crt, key))` runs, then any later `verify=True` request without `cert=` (same process, any Session or host that asks for a client certificate); or two threads with different client certs.
findings.impact: urllib3 calls `load_cert_chain()` on the passed `ssl_context`, so the module-level `_preloaded_ssl_context` keeps the client identity and presents it on later requests that never supplied it, and concurrent requests can present the wrong certificate. A local TLS server saw `['clientA', 'clientA']` at the head and `['clientA', None]` at the merge-base.
findings.change: In `_urllib3_request_context`, set `pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context` only when `client_cert is None`; otherwise let urllib3 build a per-pool context with the default bundle (for example via `ca_certs`), or use a per-cert copy of the context.

findings.title: Keep cert_verify honouring the default bundle for subclass callers
findings.trigger: An `HTTPAdapter` subclass overriding `send()` calls `self.get_connection(url)` and then `self.cert_verify(conn, url, True, cert)`, the pattern `send()` itself used before `_get_connection`.
findings.impact: `cert_verify` no longer sets `conn.ca_certs`, and `get_connection` builds a pool without the preloaded context, so urllib3 loads the OS trust store instead of certifi (`ca_certs=None` at the head, the certifi path at the merge-base). Verification stays on, but the trusted roots change silently.
findings.change: In `cert_verify`, when `verify is True` and the connection was not built with the preloaded context, still set `conn.ca_certs` to the default bundle; or document the change with migration guidance.

observations.fact: The default CA bundle is now read at `import requests`, so a missing or unreadable certifi bundle raises at import time, and the `OSError` "Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle" for `verify=True` is no longer raised in `cert_verify`.
